situation:
You are the financial analyst in the business office of WINDMERE COLLEGE, an independent college that took over ASHLAND HILL COLLEGE eighteen months ago and now runs two campuses. The vice president for finance (judge) has asked you to recommend how the college covers this quarter's payroll.

The merger is not digested. The two business offices still run on separate ledgers, so no one can say on any given morning what the combined college is owed. What is clear is that unpaid tuition balances have grown on both campuses, that payroll for both is due at the end of the quarter, and that the college must publish audited annual financial statements for its bondholders and its accreditor.

QUILLON CAPITAL has offered to buy the unpaid tuition balances at a discount and pay the college now. Selling them means the college gives up part of every dollar owed to it, permanently. QUILLON CAPITAL would then collect from the students directly, on its own terms rather than the college's. The balances sold this quarter are also the balances the college would otherwise collect next quarter, so the same gap returns larger in three months.

The other course is to leave the six open positions in the business office unfilled and postpone the ledger merge for a year. Those postings ask for the professional designations that finance staff earn through years of continuing study, and the college's own tuition support for that study is the first line the postponement takes. The two campuses would keep closing their books separately, and the audited annual statements would be late a second year.

The vice president for finance (judge) wants your recommendation and your reasoning. The vice president for finance (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the vice president for finance (judge) of WINDMERE COLLEGE. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have to fund payroll on both campuses at the end of this quarter, and neither course in front of you is comfortable. You want the financial analyst to recommend one of them — selling the unpaid tuition balances to QUILLON CAPITAL, or holding the six positions open and postponing the ledger merge — and you want to hear an honest account of the course that was left behind.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: If we go the other way instead, what do we give up?
What would that one have cost us next year?
